items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I never saw Herchel because he died before I returned to the States.

ctx.x: And when Basie introduced me the reception I received was the greatest I ever had in my career and I was so thrilled that when I spoke in the mike I offered to pay a drink for everyone there. If the public had really taken me at my word, it would have taken me a year to work out the debt to pay for all those drinks because there were at least 3000 people there.

Basie asked me who I wanted to come out front with me to assist in the rounds of solos. I was so excited that I couldn't answer. I had been an admirer of Basie's style of band since the first time I heard it on radio in Egypt in 1939. I had also heard his recording of "Blue and Sentimental" in a movie house in Egypt and didn't know until years later that it was Basie and the big tone of Herchel Evans on tenor and Prez on clarinet. I never saw Herchel because he died before I returned to the States. Basie had a…

And now, here I was on the verge of being accompanied by my favorite big band and that's all that I could think of. I should have asked for Budd Johnson and Quentin "Butter" Jackson to come out front with me because we were buddies and they had recorded with me the year before when both of them were in France with the Quincy Jones orchestra. I didn't speak up quick enough, so Basie motioned for Frank Wess and Frank Foster to come forward. Wess played flute and Foster tenor on the two numbers I did with the band…
